harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as authoritative DNS resolver for node2/node3: added an Unbound DNSBL wildcard blocklist entry for `blocked.example` returning NXDOMAIN (blocking the domain and all subdomains), applied via configctl template reload + unbound dnsbl, pointed node2/node3's NetworkManager DNS at node1's LAN IP (10.100.155.10), and verified normal resolution continues to work for all other domains. Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all three nodes with proof of changed boot identity and post-restart recovery of both the DNS service and the persisted blocking config.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD) DNS stack: confirmed unbound (unboundplus plugin) is the live resolver on port 53, dnsmasq relegated to port 53053
Located OPNsense Unbound model (config.xml OPNsense/unboundplus) and its dnsbl.blocklist array supporting wildcard domain blocking with NXDOMAIN response
Added a dnsbl blocklist entry: wildcards=blocked.example, nxdomain=1, enabled=1 to /conf/config.xml (with backup)
Regenerated templated config via `configctl template reload OPNsense/Unbound/core` and rebuilt dnsbl.json via `configctl unbound dnsbl`
Verified on node1: example.com resolves normally; blocked.example and sub.blocked.example return NXDOMAIN

Discovered node2/node3 were using the platform gateway (10.100.155.1) for DNS, not node1 - reconfigured both via nmcli (ipv4.dns=10.100.155.10, ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes) and reactivated the connection
Verified from node2 and node3: normal domains resolve, blocked.example and subdomains fail lookup (getent exit 2 / NXDOMAIN)
Captured pre-restart boot markers (FreeBSD kern.boottime on node1; /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id on node2/node3) and healthy DNS behavior baselines
Sequentially restarted node1, then node2, then node3 using native reboot (shutdown -r now backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect), polled each until exec was available again
Confirmed each node's boot identity changed post-restart and re-verified DNS service health, persisted blocklist config, and correct blocking/passing behavior after each restart

evidence.requirement: node1 provides normal name resolution for the shared private network
evidence.summary: example.com resolves correctly via node1's unbound from node1 itself, node2, and node3

evidence.requirement: blocked.example and all subdomains resolve to nothing usable from both node2 and node3
evidence.summary: getent hosts returns exit 2 (not found) for blocked.example and sub.blocked.example on node2/node3; node1 direct query shows explicit NXDOMAIN via `host`

evidence.requirement: blocking is implemented via node1's actual resolver config (not ad hoc), confirmed wildcard match covers subdomains
evidence.summary: dnsbl.json shows wildcard:true entry for blocked.example with rcode NXDOMAIN; generated unbound-blocklists.conf confirms includes.wildcards=blocked.example
Pre-restart boot marker (kern.boottime sec=1781406795) and running unbound/dnsmasq processes

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot ack returned before disconnect; connection timed out during reboot; boot time changed to sec=1788626958 confirming fresh boot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: recovered service and data
evidence.summary: Post-restart: unbound/dnsmasq running again, blocked.example/sub.blocked.example return NXDOMAIN, example.com resolves normally - config persisted

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, ack, changed boot id, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 984a7d52...; reboot ack sent; connection timed out; boot_id changed to 4997ed2a...; post-restart resolv.conf still points to node1, example.com resolves, blocked domains fail

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, ack, changed boot id, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d4784d1b...; reboot ack sent; connection errors during reboot; boot_id changed to d91aae85...; post-restart resolv.conf points to node1, example.com resolves, blocked domains fail
